text:
Alex Kim: heads-up — saw a regression on qwen-7b int8 path when FP8 kernels are enabled as fallback. 90th pct latency jumped on a subset of traces with long prefixes.
Priya Nair: hmm, is that with KV cache enabled?
Alex Kim: yes, repro with KV cache warm. baseline (int8-only) 90th=120ms, int8+fp8 fallback 90th=220ms on the same machine. CPU usage spiked on the host side.
Marc Alvarez: can you drop the perf summary? numbers / config?
Alex Kim: pasted rough microbench here:
```
model: qwen-7b
sequence: 1024 prefix + 256 gen
batching: dyn_batcher (max_batch=32, timeout=8ms)
kernels: int8 primary, fp8 fallback
kv_cache: enabled, hit_rate ~0.85
hw: a100-80gb

results:
int8-only: p50=18ms p90=120ms p99=350ms
int8+fp8-fb: p50=20ms p90=220ms p99=420ms
```
Priya Nair: interesting — KV cache hit path increases interaction between kernels when kv-copy happens. Maybe fallback kernel does an extra memcpy or different sync points.
Sasha Li: iirc FP8 path pulls a different attention kernel that materializes KV differently (we changed alignment in the fp8 rewrite). Could be cache line/packing causing stalls.
Jules Park: @perf-bot any recent regressions flagged on that commit range?
perf-bot: perf/regressions detected: commit 4f2d8a3 -> 4f9b1c0, attention-fp8-rewrite. P90 increased for qwen-7b int8+fp8 in staging. See https://perf.redwood.internal/d/attn-fp8/overview
Marc Alvarez: can someone run the small repro with tracing enabled? add kernel timestamps + cudaMemcpy counts. Use `run_trace --model qwen-7b --quant int8,fp8 --trace kernels,memcpy --prefix 1024`.
Alex Kim: running now, will upload trace.
(10 minutes later)
Alex Kim: uploaded trace to /shared/perf/qwen-int8-fp8-kv-1999.trace. quick extract:
```
# simplified trace extract
[step 1] int8_attention: forward 2.1ms
[kv_copy] cudaMemcpyAsync host->dev 0.4ms
[step 2] fp8_attention: forward 12.3ms  <-- big
[kv_merge] cudaMemcpySync dev->dev 1.8ms
[step 3] int8_output_kernel: forward 1.9ms
```
Priya Nair: that fp8_attention is the culprit. Why does the fallback take 12ms vs int8 2ms? memory layout mismatch?
Sasha Li: likely: when we fallback we re-quantize activations to fp8 on the fly and that triggers an extra rebuffering stage that isn't fused with attention. Requant + transpose may be introducing a sync.
Jules Park: for config sharing, we should produce a per-model quant profile that pins fallback kernels to avoid mixed-kernel per-step flips. e.g., force full sequence to use int8, or pre-quantize prefix into fp8 consistently.
Marc Alvarez: agreed. two mitigation options: 1) prefer consistent kernel per-request (cost maybe quality), 2) fuse re-quant + attention in fp8 path to eliminate extra memcpy/sync.
Alex Kim: temporary fix I tested: disable fp8 fallback for qwen-7b by model-profile. p90 back to 125ms (close to int8-only). small quality delta in a few eval prompts but within tolerance.
Priya Nair: can we add an automated check in profiling CI that runs small-kv-warm traces across model profiles and flags >1.5x p90 when mixing kernels?
perf-bot: new check proposal recorded: check-mixed-kernel-kv-warm. Will run on staging nightly.
Sasha Li: also we should share a sample config snippet in the model-profiles repo to help SRE and Dedicated teams. Something like:
```
quant_profiles:
  qwen-7b:
    prefer: int8
    fallback: null  # disable fp8 fallback until fused path
    batch_hint: max_batch=16, timeout=5ms
    kv_prep: prequantize_prefix: true
```
Jules Park: I'll open a PR with that and add the repro trace + perf numbers. Also adding a note to the rollout playbook: "disable mixed-kernel fallback for KV-heavy workloads until fused fp8 attention is available."
Marc Alvarez: one more ask — can we run this across other models (llama-2-13b, mistral-7b) to see if same pattern occurs? Might be specific to attention implementation.
Alex Kim: starting runs. I'll post summary when done. Thanks all. :tada:
